abstracts.abstract: This paper introduces a novel game-theoretic framework for analyzing network protocol behavior in distributed systems, representing a fundamental paradigm shift from traditional queueing-theoretic approaches. Conventional analysis methods fail to capture the strategic interactions among autonomous network entities in modern internet architecture. We propose a multi-agent game model where protocol participants rationally optimize their behavior while respecting network constraints. Our theoretical analysis establishes equilibrium conditions for protocol convergence and derives conditions for system-wide efficiency. The framework incorporates mechanism design principles to incentive-compatible protocol operation. Through rigorous mathematical derivations, we prove that our approach achieves superior modeling accuracy compared to existing techniques, particularly in scenarios involving heterogeneous network conditions and adversarial settings. The contribution extends to internet security by characterizing attack strategies and designing defensive mechanisms within a unified analytical structure. This paradigm enables systematic reasoning about complex network phenomena previously accessible only through simulation. Our results demonstrate that strategic interaction analysis fundamentally transforms the understanding of network performance, opening new research directions for protocol design and optimization.

Content delivery networks face significant challenges in predicting request latency under dynamic workload conditions, and existing analytical models provide insufficient accuracy. This paper presents an enhanced stochastic model for CDN performance analysis that substantially improves upon prior approaches. We introduce a novel correlation-aware request arrival process that captures temporal dependencies inherent in web traffic patterns, addressing a key limitation of conventional Poisson assumptions. The theoretical analysis derives closed-form expressions for key performance metrics including expected latency, cache hit rates, and tail distributions. We incorporate server heterogeneity and geographic routing effects through a hierarchical modeling approach. Rigorous proofs establish model correctness and demonstrate convergence properties. Evaluation against real-world internet measurement traces from major CDN providers validates the improved predictive accuracy, showing up to 40% error reduction compared to state-of-the-art models. The analysis provides insights for optimal cache placement strategies and load balancing in content delivery networks. This work significantly advances the theoretical foundation for web services optimization and enables more effective capacity planning in internet infrastructure.

We present EdgeChain, a novel edge computing architecture that fundamentally reimagines Internet of Things system design through decentralized intelligence. Traditional cloud-centric IoT paradigms suffer from excessive latency, privacy vulnerabilities, and single-point-of-failure risks that fundamentally constrain application potential. EdgeChain introduces a distributed ledger-based coordination mechanism that enables secure, privacy-preserving collaboration among edge nodes without central coordination. The architecture employs a hierarchical federation of edge clusters, where each cluster autonomously manages local computation while participating in global optimization through a novel consensus protocol. We design adaptive offloading algorithms that dynamically distribute computation across edge and cloud resources based on real-time conditions. The system incorporates homomorphic encryption for secure data processing in untrusted environments. Implementation experiments across diverse IoT scenarios—including smart city infrastructure and industrial automation—demonstrate that EdgeChain achieves sub-millisecond response times while maintaining strong security guarantees. This paradigm shift enables new classes of latency-sensitive applications previously infeasible under conventional architectures. The work opens fundamental new directions for internet technology research.

This paper presents SecureCompose, an enhanced framework for composing web services with significantly improved security guarantees and efficiency. Existing composition approaches inadequately address the increasingly sophisticated threat landscape facing modern distributed applications. SecureCompose introduces a multi-layered security architecture integrating formal verification, runtime monitoring, and adaptive authentication mechanisms into a unified composition framework. We design a domain-specific language that enables developers to specify security requirements alongside functional compositions, with automatic generation of enforcement policies. The system employs machine learning-based anomaly detection for runtime threat identification, achieving substantial improvements in attack detection accuracy. Performance optimization techniques reduce composition overhead by 60% compared to existing secure composition systems through intelligent caching and parallel execution strategies. The framework maintains backward compatibility with standard web services specifications while providing enhanced protection against modern attack vectors including API abuse and service impersonation. Deployment evaluation across production environments demonstrates practical applicability with minimal performance penalties. SecureCompose represents a significant advancement in building secure, composable internet services at scale.
